events.title: Samsung Internet moves to Chromium
events.summary: Samsung Internet 6.2 shipped in January 2017 on Chromium 56 — replacing the WebKit base with Blink for closer Chrome compatibility.
events.about: The Chromium switch aligned Samsung Internet with the majority of Android browsers: same DevTools quirks, extension APIs, and rendering as Chrome. It reduced web developer testing burden on Galaxy devices while keeping Samsung-specific features like content blockers.

narrative.whyChosen: Samsung Internet's Chromium migration affected hundreds of millions of Android users.
narrative.whyImportant: It consolidated mobile browsing on Blink alongside Chrome and Edge.
narrative.problemSolved: WebKit-only Samsung Internet diverged from Chrome behavior developers tested against.

sources.title: Samsung Internet Developer Docs — Chromium-based Samsung Internet

events.title: Yoshua Bengio leads founding of Mila AI institute
events.summary: Yoshua Bengio helped establish Mila — Quebec's Artificial Intelligence Institute — in January 2017, growing it into the world's largest academic deep-learning research center.
events.about: Mila consolidated Montreal's AI ecosystem under Bengio's scientific direction — attracting Element AI, corporate labs, and hundreds of researchers. It became the institutional anchor behind Bengio's Turing Award recognition.

narrative.whyChosen: Mila turned Montreal into a global deep-learning hub rivaling Silicon Valley labs.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved regional AI clusters could scale through nonprofit academic institutes.
narrative.problemSolved: Scattered university labs lacked shared compute, talent pipelines, and industry partnerships.
